_what_this_is: The human rulings register. Every design decision the USER made, in the user's own words, with the date and the session it was said in. A ruling is not a feature and not a plan - it is a thing the user settled that the build is not free to re-derive. Declining a ruling is allowed; forgetting one is not.
_why_it_exists: Ruling RL-019 was given on 2026-08-17 after the user found that a design they had settled on 2026-08-03 was only 2/22 built. The pattern behind it: rulings were recorded as prose inside whichever document was open at the time, or not at all, so nothing could enumerate them and nothing could measure whether the running system honoured them. Section 3a of the goal document is the counter-example that worked - the ruling was written verbatim the moment it was given.
_how_status_is_decided: It is NOT decided here. No row carries a status field on purpose. Each row names a probe; statuswall.ruling_conformance runs it and the board renders what it measured. A ruling with probe:null renders NOT MEASURED, never green (Rule 8). Typing a status into this file would be exactly the fiction the board exists to prevent.
_source_note: Rows sourced 'transcript' were recovered on 2026-08-17 from ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl by reading every user message in the project's history. Verbatim text is reproduced as typed, including typos - it is the user's wording, not a cleaned-up paraphrase, because a paraphrase is how the meaning drifts.

rulings.verbatim: now make the brains real ai not rule based
rulings.clarified_as: The BULL, BEAR and PROFIT-TAIL brains of every segment decide from TRAINED MODELS, not stated thresholds. Every numeric parameter in the decision path traces to a fit() with a logged loss and a dataset reference (§1a L1). Chosen in interview: the model drives paper trading immediately - RL-005 makes paper the place for unrestricted experiment and no capital is at risk - while the promotion gate governs any future real-money step. Learning happens in two labelled places: a supervised retrainer refits from the store on a cadence (scheduled retraining), and the LIVE loop updates its own calibration and conformal abstention threshold from realised outcomes every poll (§1a L2).
rulings.means: RL-025's rule brains were scaffolding and this is their replacement, not their extension. A brain that cannot name the fit that produced its numbers is not admissible.

rulings.verbatim: also lots of futer featues and intelliences learnin will be connectin to tis
rulings.clarified_as: The learned brain layer is an EXTENSION POINT, not one model wired to one engine. Future intelligence capabilities - the ten §1a.6 orders first, and whatever follows - attach as belief sources and belief critics without modifying the engine, the arbiter or the segment bots. The carrier is a BELIEF: a claim with its provenance, its epistemic class (read / verified / observed, and only observed may size a position) and a half-life after which it expires rather than being silently reused.
rulings.means: Any capability that cannot be expressed as a belief with provenance, class and expiry does not attach here, and any decision path that reads a raw model output instead of a belief has bypassed the extension point.

rulings.verbatim: also new feature for every sement bots i need te usdt profit or loss for te captal used or ow muc capital orusdt by bot tradin ow muc profit it ot in usdt
rulings.clarified_as: Every segment bot reports, in USDT, how much capital it used and how much profit or loss it made on it. Asked how capital should be counted the user chose ALL THREE SIDE BY SIDE: PEAK CONCURRENT NOTIONAL (the most USDT at risk at one moment - what the bot needed), CUMULATIVE NOTIONAL TRADED (turnover, the same dollar counted every round trip), and EQUITY AGAINST A DECLARED BANKROLL per bot (a real account's view). No single one of the three is allowed to stand alone as 'return', because each answers a different question and the three differ by orders of magnitude.
rulings.means: A P&L figure with no capital beside it is not a result, and a return computed against an unstated capital base is a number chosen to flatter. Every tile carries all three denominators or it carries none.

rulings.verbatim: [interview answer] Convert to USDT at the live BTC price, rate journalled per fill
rulings.clarified_as: Deribit options are quoted in BTC, not USDT. The options bot converts its premiums to USDT at the LIVE BTC mark so all four bots are comparable in one currency, and the rate used is journalled with each fill so any converted figure can be audited back to the price it was converted at.
rulings.means: A converted number whose rate was not recorded cannot be checked, and mixing a BTC-denominated P&L into a USDT total without conversion is a unit error that looks like a result. A fill with no rate recorded may not be converted at all - it reports as unconvertible rather than being converted at a rate nobody saw.

_how_scope_works: Every ruling binds at a level, and the level decides the denominator the reconciliation counts against: per-segment needs a row in all four segment slices, per-brain in all twelve brains, shared and system need one row anywhere. Assigned once is not resolved four times - that is how a cross-cutting capability reads as done while three of four bots never received it. Default assignment (spec 2026-08-17 §5): decides about a symbol or market -> per-segment; about a brain's own learning, beliefs or competence -> per-brain; about capture, store, cost, validation, registry, tail cap or governance -> shared; whole-account objective -> system.
